title: Desktop audio player with screen-reader-only, opacity, and visibility hidden UI
stressor: hidden UI that must emit no runs: 1px sr-only clip, opacity:0 ancestor, visibility:hidden, clip-rect and clip-path(inset 50%) offscreen text
notes: Self-contained single page, all CSS inline, no script, no network URLs. Reproduces the desktop audio-player fault class the hidden-box filter targets. Visible content emits runs: an h1, two paragraphs, and a player bar with Play, a time readout, and Volume. The hidden set must emit zero runs: a .sr-only block using the 1px clip pattern (absolute position, 1px width/height, overflow hidden, clip rect) plus opacity:0, carrying a volume-keys hint sentence; a speed menu (1.75x down to 0.75x) whose items carry opacity:0; a tooltip hidden with visibility:hidden; a MediaElement.js .mejs-offscreen clone using clip rect(1px,1px,1px,1px) plus clip-path:inset(50%) (no opacity, no visibility); a clip-rect-only span using clip rect(0,0,0,0) alone; a clip-path-only span using clip-path:inset(50%) alone. The filter drops on visibility:hidden, on effective opacity at or near zero, and on clip-offscreen (an absolute or fixed box whose clip rect collapses or whose clip-path is inset(50%)). The forcing stylesheet sets line-height:cellH on every element, so a subpixel-height page box still reports a full cell tall; the sr-only hint therefore relies on its own opacity:0, and the clip-offscreen set on its collapsed clip, not the 1px clip's height, to drop. The hidden strings use distinctive text so a capture inspection can grep them (the exact speed labels, the volume-keys hint, the tooltip text, and the clip-offscreen hint sentences).
